newsitem.title: GERMANY: German aluminium processors declare bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: German aluminium processors declare bankruptcy.

text.p: Three more aluminium processing plants owned by the private Gottschol group opened bankruptcy proceedings after its eastern German plant Rackwitz Aluminium AG did so on Tuesday, local law courts said.

The court in Schwelm, North-Rhine Westphalia, said Gottschol Aluminium GmbH in Ennepetal and its subsidiary in Nachrodt filed for bankruptcy after they could no longer meet their financial oblications.
Courts in Berlin received a similar declaration from Gottschol Metalwerke GmbH and Co.
Rackwitz cited an aluminium demand lull and start-up problems with new machinery.
Possible job losses at the four plants amount to 950.
Gottschol, which apart from Rackwitz operates seven plants in western Germany, focuses on aluminium products for the building and construction sectors.
An analyst said the companies may have fallen victim to overcapacity at firms making continuously cast billets and casting alloys amid a building industry slowdown.
Demand for such aluminium products had been weak but was holding up in other applications such as transport.
Receivers have not yet been appointed for the Enneptal, Nachrodt and Berlin plants. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
